newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq wants U.N. to probe into sport case with Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Iraq wants U.N. to probe into sport case with Lebanon.

text.p: An Iraqi newspaper on Saturday demanded that a complaint be lodged in a United Nations court against Lebanon for preventing Iraqi athletes from taking part in the Pan Arab Games which begin in Beirut on Saturday.

"The (Iraqi) Olympics Committee is required to protect Iraq and its athletes' right through lodging a case in the International Court of Justice against the ad hoc committee of the Pan Arab games," al-Baath al-Riyadhi (Sports) newspaper said in an editorial.
The 97 Iraqi athletes have been waiting since Friday at a Lebanese frontier post after Lebanon refused to let them enter the country to compete in the games.
"Let the whole world know that Iraq's right will not forfeit and it will defend it through international laws and conventions," the paper said.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya lashed out at Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, blaming them for the Lebanese decision of excluding Iraq from the games.
"What Kuwaiti and Saudi circles are doing represents a flagrant violation (against Iraq)...which is unacceptable whatsoever," the paper said.
A Lebanese foreign ministry official said on Wednesday Beirut was under pressure from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to exclude the Iraqis from the games.
"The aggression committed by Saudi and Kuwait princes and sheikhs against Iraq in the Arab games will not be forgotten by Iraqis," Jumhouriya said.
